blocks.text: Why sound matters
Clip → Source → Listener → Mixer
Play vs PlayOneShot
2D vs 3D: Spatial Blend and distance
AudioMixer: groups and routing
Where audio goes wrong
A scene can look right and still feel dead.
Sound tells the player where things are, what just happened, and how dangerous it is.
Today is not a tour of every audio property.
It is four decisions: 2D or 3D, Play or PlayOneShot, which mixer group, and how far the sound carries.
In the lab you will walk around a small scene and hear the difference.
Four pieces, one path:
AudioClip — the sound file
AudioSource — the component that plays it
AudioListener — the ears; one per scene, usually on the Main Camera
AudioMixer — the routing board that controls groups and effects
Clip → Source → Listener: the sound travels through 3D space
Source → Mixer → Master: the volume and effects are applied
Play() replaces the current clip on that source — one sound at a time. PlayOneShot(clip) layers the clip on top — many overlapping sounds from one source.
Use Play for music and loops; use PlayOneShot for footsteps, gunshots, and pickups.
Randomise pitch slightly on repeated one-shots, or they sound like a machine gun.
Spatial Blend 0 — 2D: same volume everywhere; use for UI, music, narration
Spatial Blend 1 — 3D: volume and pan depend on the listener's position; use for footsteps, ambience, in-world effects
Min Distance — inside this radius the source is at full volume
Max Distance — beyond this radius it is silent
Rolloff — how fast it fades between the two; Logarithmic feels natural
Footstep: Min 1, Max 15. Campfire: Min 2, Max 30.
public AudioClip[] clips;
public AudioSource source;
private float nextStep;
void Update()
bool moving = Mathf.Abs(Input.GetAxisRaw("Horizontal")) > 0.1f
|| Mathf.Abs(Input.GetAxisRaw("Vertical")) > 0.1f;
if (moving && Time.time >= nextStep)
source.pitch = Random.Range(0.9f, 1.1f);
source.PlayOneShot(clips[Random.Range(0, clips.Length)]);
nextStep = Time.time + 0.4f;
An AudioMixer is a tree: Master → BGM / SFX → sub-groups
Each group has volume in dB, pitch, and an effects chain
A source routes to a group through its Output field
If Output is None, the source bypasses the mixer — sliders and effects do nothing
Expose a group volume to script and drive it from a settings slider
One SFX slider lowers every footstep and gunshot at once
Check these before asking for help:
I hear nothing — no AudioListener, volume 0, or a missing clip
3D source is silent right next to it — Min Distance is too large; you are inside the "silent" zone
Changing the mixer slider does nothing — the source's Output is still None
Footsteps sound like a machine gun — no throttle, or Play instead of PlayOneShot
Crackling — too many overlapping one-shots; lower the volume or add a Compressor
Four decisions, one scene.
2D or 3D — choose the role
Play or PlayOneShot — choose the channel
Which mixer group — choose the category
How far it carries — Min/Max Distance
Lab: three 3D sources, one BGM source, an AudioMixer, and a footsteps script. Walk around and listen.
Next week: VFX — the same "make it, then judge it" workflow, with your eyes.
